checks.description: The home-ground tier changes at least one field choice. On 16:9 the ground-blind score sent four harvesters from a ~2,000-credit home field to a 13,160-credit frontier field 34 cells out at 279-282s, and both replacements after them. If this id is absent, either IsFrontier never classified a field as frontier (mirror or sighting anchor wrong) or no frontier field outscored home ground, and nothing about harvester survival can be attributed to this round.

A harvester on frontier fallback ground comes home only when home ground worth half its field returns, and never goes back while home ground lasts. Each economy.harvester-leaves-frontier is a real order; more than 30 in a match means the frontier classification is flipping or the rule is oscillating.

Own harvesters (owner=Commander; without it enemy harvesters count as zero-lifetime rows) lived 194.8s on average here, all six dying 379-405s on the road from the frontier field. Kept on home ground they should outlive one raid.
525 of 877 seconds had no live harvester after the frontier wipe. The round before the survey had it at 118.

Lifetime income was 16.0 c/s against a prior median of 38.3, because earnings froze at 14,075 from ~400s. Home-ground-first can cost some rate while home fields thin; losing the fleet cost everything after 405s.
meanArmyValue was 783.8 against a prior median of 1,683.5; the army peaked at 3,120 before the economy died.
Fitness was 0.226 against a prior median of 0.634. Diagnostic only; paired benchmark results decide promotion.
